subject: Film & Cinema
title: The Three-Act Structure
description: A quick, practical guide to The Three-Act Structure.

hook.text: Almost every Hollywood film follows the same invisible skeleton: setup, confrontation, resolution.

buildup.text: Act one introduces the world and characters. Act two creates obstacles. Act three resolves them.

discovery.text: This structure dates back to Aristotle's Poetics — it's thousands of years old.

twist.text: Many acclaimed films deliberately break this structure to surprise audiences.

climax.text: Knowing the rules lets writers choose when and how to break them effectively.

punchline.text: The oldest story formula still works.

quiz.question: What are the three acts in the classic film structure?
